principle: Refactoring UI — Color & hierarchy; Material 3 color roles; brief: dashboard stat colours (time=purple, streak=yellow, completion=green, active=cyan)
location: src/components/kit/StatBox.tsx (number div) via src/lib/cn.ts twMerge — affects every StatBox on /dashboard and /projects/[id]
problem: The just-shipped dashboard stat colours do NOT render. Live computed color of all four stat numbers (07 / 3% / 02 / 0:00) is rgb(255,255,255) white. The rendered class list is 'font-display text-3xl leading-none lg:text-4xl text-glow-cyan' — text-glow-cyan (the glow) is present but the accentText class (text-cyan/green/yellow/purple) has been STRIPPED. Root cause is tailwind-merge: cn() = twMerge(clsx(...)) treats both 'text-cyan' and 'text-glow-cyan' as the same 'text-color' group, so last-wins drops 'text-cyan' and keeps only the glow. Reproduced in isolation: cn('...','text-cyan','text-glow-cyan') => '... text-glow-cyan' (colour gone). Numbers get a cyan text-shadow on white text. Headline batch item is silently neutralised at runtime.
fix: Register the custom glow utilities with tailwind-merge so it stops grouping them with text-color. In src/lib/cn.ts replace twMerge with an extended instance: const twMerge = extendTailwindMerge({ extend: { classGroups: { 'text-glow': [{ 'text-glow': ['cyan','green','yellow','purple','red','orange'] }] } } }). Alternatively apply the glow via plain clsx outside the twMerge color group, or set colour via inline style. Verify live: stat number computed color must equal --color-cyan #00d2ff (active), --color-green #51fd80 (completion), --color-yellow #eef996 (streak), --color-purple #9b80dc (time).

principle: Color is not the only channel; brief: PROJECTS priority dropdown coloured by priority (Red/orange/Yellow)
location: src/lib/palette.ts (--color-orange utility) — PriorityDropdown 'MED' trigger on /projects table + /projects/[id] PRIORITY cell; src/components/kit/Listbox.tsx accentBorder/accentText['orange']
problem: Priority colour-coding is half-broken. Med priority maps to 'orange' (priorityAccent.Med = 'orange'), but text-orange and border-orange resolve to rgb(255,255,255) white at runtime — measured live on the real MED trigger (class list includes 'text-orange' yet computed color AND border are both white). By contrast text-red (#ff4242) and text-yellow (#eef996) resolve correctly, so High renders red and Low renders yellow, but MED renders white. Because MED is the default priority, most project rows show a colourless white priority control. --color-orange:#ff9d3c IS declared in @theme but Tailwind v4 does not emit a working bare text-orange/border-orange utility the way it does for the overridden red token (collides with TW's built-in shaded orange palette).
fix: Make the orange token emit real utilities. Easiest: rename the token so it doesn't collide with Tailwind's default orange palette — add --color-amber: #ff9d3c in @theme and point priorityAccent.Med + the Accent type at 'amber' (text-amber/border-amber). Or declare explicit @utility text-orange { color: var(--color-orange); } and @utility border-orange { border-color: var(--color-orange); } in globals.css. Verify: MED trigger computed color === #ff9d3c.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow; Refactoring UI spacing/grouping; brief: mobile section
location: src/components/tools/* Color Wheel 'HARMONY · CLOSEST PAINTS' rows — /tools/wheel at 390px
problem: On the Color Wheel at 390px the 'closest paints' result rows overlap: the ASSIGN dropdown text is rendered on top of the paint brand labels ('WARCOLOURS', 'MONUMENT HOBBIES'), so both are unreadable. The row keeps its desktop horizontal layout (swatch -> name+brand -> ASSIGN) instead of stacking, so the fixed-width ASSIGN control collides with the brand name. Desktop renders the identical section perfectly — mobile-only. The sibling Color Stacking tool's ramp rows DO reflow correctly at 390px (reference pattern).
fix: Make the closest-paints row reflow at narrow widths: wrap in flex-wrap or switch to a stacked grid under ~480px (swatch + name/brand on row 1, ASSIGN full-width on row 2), mirroring the Color Stacking ramp-row layout which already works at 390px. Ensure ASSIGN gets its own line and the brand label is not overlapped.

principle: Shopify Polaris — empty states; WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow; brief: mobile + empty states
location: src/components/collection/* MY MODEL COLLECTION empty state — /collection at 390px
problem: The 'MY MODEL COLLECTION' empty state clips off the right edge at 390px: the empty message reads 'NO M…' (truncated, should be 'NO MODELS…') and an inline '+ A…' add CTA is cut off by the viewport. The empty-state block does not reflow to the mobile column, so a new user's first-run model-collection state shows a clipped headline and a half-hidden action. The paint-collection block directly above reflows fine.
fix: Constrain the model-collection empty state to the mobile column: remove the fixed/min width causing the horizontal clip, let the 'NO MODELS YET' text wrap, and make the add CTA full-width (a full-width '+ ADD MODEL' already exists at the panel bottom — the clipped inline one appears to be a second, non-reflowing copy). Match the paint-collection empty-state treatment which renders correctly.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 Info & Relationships / §2.4.6 Headings; heading order h1->h2->h3 no skips
location: project-detail (/projects/[id]) — project name renders as <h2> with no <h1>; /projects (mobile) reuses dashboard <h1>DASHBOARD
problem: Heading order issues. (a) The project-detail inspector's top heading is an <h2> ('QA Order Mobile …') with no <h1> on the page — the document outline starts at h2, a skip that breaks the screen-reader outline. (b) /projects renders <h1>DASHBOARD (it is the dashboard view), so the page title heading reads 'DASHBOARD' on a route the user navigated to as Projects.
fix: (a) Promote the project name on project-detail to <h1> (keep the visual style, change only the tag) so the page has a single top-level heading; section headings (Recipe, Sub-projects, Notes) remain h2/h3. (b) Optional: if /projects should read as Projects, set its h1 text to 'PROJECTS' not 'DASHBOARD'.

location: Text <input> fields app-wide (22px tall): /sign-in, /sign-up, /collection, /library, /focus, /recipes, /tools/match, project-detail; plus library 'Hue coverage map' button (316x2px)
problem: Two target-size misses at mobile. (a) Text inputs render 22px tall (sign-in/up 274x22, collection URL 324x22, focus 208x22), 2px under the WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 24px minimum. They are full-width (easy to hit horizontally) but the vertical hit area is sub-minimum. (b) The Library 'Hue coverage map' toggle measures 316x2px — a 2px-tall hit target (collapsed/zero-height control), effectively untappable.
fix: (a) Bump shared kit input / Listbox-trigger min-height to >=24px (ideally 44px for comfortable touch). (b) Investigate the library 'Hue coverage map' button rendering at 2px tall — give it an explicit min-height >=24px or fix the collapsed layout so it's tappable.

principle: Vintage Terminal/CRT §9 — tabular-nums / glyph alignment; Refactoring UI typography
location: StatBox 'Time Total' value + project-detail TIME stat — the pixel 'X:XX' colon glyph
problem: The Time Total value 'X:XX' shows the colon glyph overlapping/crowding adjacent digits in the pixel display font at the 3xl/4xl size (reads as a smudge). Cosmetic, but it is the one stat that looks slightly broken next to the clean digit-only boxes.
fix: Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (or a small letter-spacing) to the StatBox value when it contains ':' so the time reads on the character grid like the other trackers.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency & standards; Refactoring UI — affordance
location: project-detail (/projects/[id]) TYPE field vs STATUS/PRIORITY dropdowns
problem: On the project-detail inspector, TYPE renders as a green solid-bordered box ('UNIT') in the same row as STATUS and PRIORITY which are dotted-border dropdowns. The three look like they should behave the same, but TYPE appears static/read-only styled as an input — an affordance mismatch in a row of otherwise-interactive controls.
fix: If TYPE is read-only, restyle it as a label/value (drop the input-like solid border). If editable, convert it to the same dotted-border Listbox the STATUS/PRIORITY cells use.

principle: Vintage Terminal/CRT §9 — pure-black halation caveat (deliberate choice, noted not flagged)
problem: The canvas background is now pure #000000 (the blue cast was successfully removed — batch item landed). Per §9 of the rubric, pure black can cause halation (bright phosphor text blooming into a halo) for users with astigmatism and on OLED. The rubric recommends #0D0D0D-#111111 for the base. This is a deliberate aesthetic decision, logged as a trade-off to monitor, not a defect. Near-black raised surfaces (#0d0d0f panels) are fine.
fix: No action required unless halation is reported. If softening is ever wanted, set --color-bg to #0a0a0a-#0d0d0d (keeps the no-blue-cast look while reducing OLED halation). Keep as-is for the intended pure-black terminal aesthetic.
